status: Unproved proof route; no caller grant and no accepted paper
motivation: Printed endpoints are rational but barycentric coefficients and centers may be real. The discontinuous function0 on Q and -1 off Q satisfies every printed PCC inequality. Paper225 contains the complete direct proof but is not yet independently accepted. Its explicit-continuity maximum principle therefore cannot simply be granted for all printed PC functions.
intended_new_statement: For a positive balanced finite rational space, a rational-endpoint PC function locally bounded above and below may have a unique continuous PC representative agreeing at every rational point and dominating the original function at irrational centers. For a continuous obstacle with a continuous PA PC reference and bounded relative obstacle, the exact printed PC envelope should equal the continuous-competitor envelope and be continuous. This is not a real-PA regularization theorem or contact classification.
proposed_proof_steps: Use max(q,gamma+inf(u)) to replace each envelope competitor by one above a common continuous lower barrier, still below gamma+u and satisfying every rational-endpoint PCC inequality. This gives uniform two-sided bounds m,M on each compact local chart. No automatic continuity of q is assumed.

At a relative face tau, choose rational z in relint(tau), a fixed set of rational local-star generators v_i, positive rational kernel coefficients lambda_i and epsilon>0 with z+epsilon*v_i in incident faces. On a compact subset of relint(tau) these choices should be uniform in z. Establish this finite-polyhedral geometry carefully; it is not a granted lemma.

For rational y in an incident face write y-z=sum a_i*v_i with a_i>=0 and sum a_i<=C*norm(y-z), using a finite simplicial subdivision modulo lineality. The barycentric combination of z and z+epsilon*v_i inside that face gives the upper bound q(y)-q(z)<=C*(M-m)*norm(y-z). Verify sum a_i/epsilon<=1 on the small neighborhood and the exact PCC face constraints.

The positive kernel relation from225 suggests z is a PCC of y and z+epsilon*v_i with unnormalized y coefficient1 and other coefficients (t*lambda_i-a_i)/epsilon>=0. Choose t=max_i(a_i/lambda_i)=O(norm(y-z)). The sum of other coefficients is O(norm(y-z)), so Jensen yields q(y)-q(z)>=-C*(M-m)*norm(y-z). All endpoints are rational. Derive constants uniform as z ranges near an irrational point of tau.

On rational points of a relative-face interior, ordinary rational convexity plus local two-sided bounds gives a unique continuous convex extension, with common local Lipschitz bounds. Combine that face extension with the preceding transverse estimates to obtain a continuous extension across all incident faces. This is the main missing recognition lemma; do not replace it with a source automatic-continuity citation.

For an arbitrary irrational center x, rational simplices in its relative face give q(x)<=q_bar(x) through the actual rational-endpoint PCC inequalities and continuous convergence of the vertex values. The extension agrees with q at rational points but does not force equality at irrational points.

To prove q_bar satisfies the printed PCC inequality at every real center, fix rational endpoints and approximate feasible real barycentric coefficients by rational feasible coefficients. The feasible set imposes sum(alpha)=1, alpha>=0 and the center in the rational face tau, hence is a rational polyhedron. Check rational density within its actual face; limiting centers stay in tau. For all-real endpoints, a homogenized perspective polyhedron in (alpha_i,t_i=alpha_i*x_i) might provide an analogous argument, but that stronger assertion is optional and unproved.

For a continuous obstacle, q_bar<=gamma+u by rational density and the continuous obstacle. The original one-sided growth bound also passes to q_bar. Thus q_bar is itself a valid printed competitor. Apply the lemma directly to the supremum P, which inherits the rational PCC inequalities and the same common two-sided bounds. Since P_bar is a valid competitor and dominates P, maximality gives P=P_bar at all points.

This would justify continuity and the correct continuous competitor envelope despite the printed PC-class pathology. It would not produce uniform global real-PA approximants, a genuine extended MA operator, or the missing higher-dimensional local contact theorem. Those original gaps remain explicit.
possible_structural_next_step: For finite PA germs, investigate the raw top-intersection polynomial on faces of the local polyhedral-convexity cone where a nonnegative PCC relation is tight. A structural contact criterion might require vanishing on every locally/global-growth-realizable tight face. This is only a research question: neither sufficiency/necessity nor global gamma realization nor operator continuity has been proved. Avoid a tautological restatement of envelope orthogonality.
